input.rationale: Registered the successor execution for the lost-decision discriminator: the harness adds a lost_acknowledged_commit case on a three-voter committed configuration. The leader first demotes both peers (committed single-voter configuration), applies 100 commands, snapshots that configuration, then promotes both peers back to voters (committed three-voter configuration). Every instance is stopped, the former leader is restarted, and if it is running it acknowledges one commit with a unique payload; the holder is then stopped, the other two voters are restarted with the flag disabled, and the payload is looked for on every store, including after the holder rejoins. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the restarted instance held one voter against its log's three, elected itself alone and acknowledged the commit, which afterwards existed on exactly one copy with the other two voters never having received it; with the flag disabled it reconstructed the three-voter configuration, elected nobody and acknowledged nothing ("node is not the leader").

scope.description: Whether an acknowledged commit taken on a reconstructed smaller configuration is durable on a majority of the committed configuration. Nine in-process cases: the seven previously exercised restart shapes plus a lost_acknowledged_commit case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is left with a single voter, snapshotted, then made three voters again; after every instance is stopped the former leader is restarted, the instance acknowledges one uniquely named commit, the holder is stopped, the other two voters are restarted with the flag disabled, and every store is scanned for that payload before and after the holder rejoins.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across restarts.
The committed configuration of the lost_acknowledged_commit case has three voters while the node's own snapshot metadata carries the demoted configuration with one voter.

The two voters brought back after the acknowledged commit are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs and the second leadership is formed by a majority that never held the payload.
The acknowledged commit is attempted with a 1500 ms timeout, leadership waits use the 3000 ms window, and the payload is searched for across first-index to last-index of each store.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, membership changes after the acknowledged commit, and any comparison of payload contents beyond the exact unique byte string.

experiment.prefix: The new case runs after the earlier cases in the same test. It builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), calls leader.DemoteVoter on both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), then calls leader.AddVoter for both peers with their addresses and applies five more entries. It emits a lost_inputs CA_EVENT with the last configuration entry (index, decoded server list, voter count), the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and voter count, and the tracked commit index; it then stops every instance and rebuilds the former leader over its own stores with a fresh in-memory transport. After a bounded leadership wait it applies one uniquely named payload, records whether the future completed and the index it returned, and stops that instance. It rebuilds the other two peers with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled over their own stores, connects the rebuilt instances in both directions, waits for one of them to become leader, and scans both stores for the payload; it then rebuilds the original holder the same way, waits, and scans again. It emits an entry_survival CA_EVENT carrying the reconstructed voter count, the acknowledgement outcome, the payload index, whether the payload remains on the holder after the rejoin, how many of the other voters hold it, the derived durable_on_majority with the copy count, and both terms.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; the committed configuration recorded in the node's own log is the basis on which a client acknowledgement is supposed to be durable.

comparisons.description: Three-voter case with the flag enabled: the reconstructed voter count is compared with the number of voters in the configuration entry persisted in the node's own log.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the reconstructed voter count matches the committed configuration entry.
Three-voter case with the flag enabled: an acknowledged commit is expected to be durable on a majority of the committed configuration rather than on a single copy.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the single running member of a three-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the three-voter lost_acknowledged_commit case with its flag-disabled control: demote both peers, snapshot the single-voter configuration, promote both peers again, restart the former leader, acknowledge one uniquely named commit on it, then bring the other two voters back and scan every store for that payload. Replaces the comparison set with this case's reconstruction and durability predicates.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

basis.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the second shape calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) plus 10 more applies. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list) together with the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. Each emitted CA_EVENT JSON line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity, plus raw operands (latest_config_index, log_config_index, snapshot_config_index and the server lists), the instance's own configuration, the public GetConfiguration view, last_applied, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election attempts and became_leader over the 3000 ms window.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.

comparisons.description: Control for the no-snapshot shape: with restore committed logs disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index should equal the index of the configuration entry persisted in its own log.

No-snapshot shape with restore committed logs enabled and the configuration entry inside the applied prefix: the restored instance's latest configuration index is compared with the configuration entry index in its own log.
Control for the snapshot-then-remove shape: with the flag disabled the restarted voter should pick up the configuration entry committed after the snapshot.

Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the configuration entry committed after the snapshot lies inside the applied prefix, and the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with it.

Identifies the origin of the reconstructed value: whether the restarted instance's configuration server set equals the configuration carried by its own snapshot metadata rather than the configuration entry in its log.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the no-snapshot shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when restore committed logs is disabled.
No-snapshot shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the snapshot-then-remove shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when the flag is disabled.
Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed single-voter configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: five in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities. Two single-voter shapes (no snapshot; snapshot then a committed RemoveServer of the non-leader peer) are each run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled, and a fifth case repeats the snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled but nothing dispatched after the removal, so the committed configuration entry stays above the commit index the restart replays. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, reads the configuration entry, tracked commit index and snapshot metadata from the surviving instance's own stores, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In every shape the committed configuration after setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration with no snapshot, or the configuration left by a committed RemoveServer that follows a snapshot, while the snapshot metadata still names two voters.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms), and every flag-enabled case is paired with a flag-disabled control or with the within-flag case.

The fifth case relies on the tracked commit index lagging the committed configuration entry when nothing is dispatched after the removal; the actual values are emitted as staged_commit_index and log_config_index in its restart_inputs event.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

experiments.revision_reason: The restart_observation event now emits the config_entry_in_applied_prefix operand (with last_applied and log_config_index) so the configuration-reconstruction comparisons can evaluate, and a fifth within-flag case was added in which the committed configuration entry stays above the replayed committed prefix (staged commit index 102 versus entry index 103), separating the skipped configuration entry from the flag's own committed-log replay as the cause of the observed non-progress.

scope.description: Whether a reconstructed configuration smaller than the committed one changes which support counts. Seven in-process cases: the five previously exercised restart shapes (no-snapshot, snapshot-then-RemoveServer, and the within-flag case whose configuration entry stays above the replayed prefix) plus a new shape in which the snapshot records one voter because the second peer was demoted before it and the committed configuration afterwards has two voters because the peer was promoted again after it; that shape runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In the new shape, after the bounded leadership wait the other instance is stopped and one entry is committed with a 1000 ms Apply timeout, so the support the completed decision rested on is observable.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no membership change is issued after it.
In the new shape the committed configuration has two voters after the promotion while the node's own snapshot metadata still carries the demoted configuration with a single voter.

Every instance of the cluster is stopped before the restart in each case, so after the restart the other member is unavailable in the new shape as well and the surviving instance is the only member of the committed configuration that is running.
The bounded leadership window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms) and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, restarting more than one member, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.

result.summary: Built and registered the lost-decision probe the current discriminator called for: a successor execution whose harness adds a three-voter lost_acknowledged_commit case (demote both peers to leave one voter, snapshot that configuration, promote both peers back to voters, stop everything, restart the former leader, acknowledge one uniquely named commit on it, then bring the other two voters back with the flag disabled and scan every store for that payload before and after the holder rejoins). Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the restarted instance reconstructed one voter against its log's three, elected itself alone and acknowledged the payload, which afterwards existed on exactly one copy with the other two voters never having received it; with the flag disabled it reconstructed the three-voter configuration and acknowledged nothing ("node is not the leader"). Four comparisons are declared: reconstructed voter count against the log's configuration entry with its control, and the acknowledged commit's durability on a majority of the committed configuration with its control; validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so this turn recorded no interpretation, and the probe does not yet show the acknowledged copy being discarded (the holder still carries it after rejoining), so that stronger consequence remains unestablished.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

It then waits up to 3000 ms for leadership, and in the new shape stops the other instance and calls Apply with a 1000 ms timeout, recording apply_ok, apply_error and apply_ms. Each emitted CA_EVENT line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity plus latest_config_index, latest_config_voters, the server sets, log_config_index, log_config_voters, snapshot_config_index, last_applied, staged_commit_index, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election_requests, became_leader and the commit outcome.

before.description: Control for the no-snapshot shape: with restore committed logs disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index should equal the index of the configuration entry persisted in its own log.

No-snapshot shape with restore committed logs enabled and the configuration entry inside the replayed committed prefix: the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with the configuration entry index in its own log.
Control for the snapshot-then-remove shape: with the flag disabled the restarted voter should pick up the configuration entry committed after the snapshot.

Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the configuration entry committed after the snapshot lies inside the replayed committed prefix, and the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with it.

Identifies the origin of the reconstructed value: whether the restarted instance's configuration server set equals the configuration carried by its own snapshot metadata rather than the configuration entry in its log.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the no-snapshot shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when restore committed logs is disabled.
No-snapshot shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the snapshot-then-remove shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when the flag is disabled.
Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed single-voter configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.

Within-flag control: with the flag enabled but the committed configuration entry above the replayed committed prefix, the restarted instance's latest configuration index should still equal the configuration entry index in its own log.
Within-flag control for progress: with the flag enabled and the configuration entry above the replayed committed prefix, the restarted sole voter reaches Leader inside the bounded window.

after.description: New shape with the flag enabled: the reconstructed number of voters is compared with the number of voters in the configuration entry persisted in the node's own log.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the reconstructed voter count matches the committed configuration entry.
New shape with the flag enabled: the instance acquired leadership without sending any election request to another member, while its own log's configuration has two voters.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the instance does seek support from the other member of the committed two-voter configuration.

New shape with the flag enabled: one entry is committed while the other member of the committed configuration is stopped, so the completed decision rested on support that is not a majority of the committed configuration.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the same commit attempt does not complete while the other member is stopped, because the committed configuration requires both voters.
In-run control: the established divergence reproduces in this run (empty configuration against the single-voter entry at log index 1).
In-run control: the established divergence reproduces in this run (the snapshot's two-voter configuration against the single-voter entry at log index 103).

experiments.revision_reason: Adds the voter_promoted_after_snapshot case (demote the non-leader peer, snapshot, promote it again) with a decision-duty step that stops the other instance and commits one entry, restores transport connectivity with still-running peers after the restart, emits election_requests and the commit outcome, and replaces the comparison set with the safety-direction predicates plus two established divergence predicates as in-run controls.

scope.description: Whether an acknowledged commit taken on a reconstructed smaller configuration is durable on a majority of the committed configuration. Nine in-process cases: the seven previously exercised restart shapes plus a lost_acknowledged_commit case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is left with a single voter, snapshotted, then made three voters again; after every instance is stopped the former leader is restarted, the instance acknowledges one uniquely named commit, the holder is stopped, the other two voters are restarted with the flag disabled, and every store is scanned for that payload before and after the holder rejoins.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across restarts.
The committed configuration of the lost_acknowledged_commit case has three voters while the node's own snapshot metadata carries the demoted configuration with one voter.

The two voters brought back after the acknowledged commit are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs and the second leadership is formed by a majority that never held the payload.
The acknowledged commit is attempted with a 1500 ms timeout, leadership waits use the 3000 ms window, and the payload is searched for across first-index to last-index of each store.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, membership changes after the acknowledged commit, and any comparison of payload contents beyond the exact unique byte string.

basis.prefix: The new case runs after the earlier cases in the same test. It builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), calls leader.DemoteVoter on both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), then calls leader.AddVoter for both peers with their addresses and applies five more entries. It emits a lost_inputs CA_EVENT with the last configuration entry (index, decoded server list, voter count), the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and voter count, and the tracked commit index; it then stops every instance and rebuilds the former leader over its own stores with a fresh in-memory transport. After a bounded leadership wait it applies one uniquely named payload, records whether the future completed and the index it returned, and stops that instance. It rebuilds the other two peers with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled over their own stores, connects the rebuilt instances in both directions, waits for one of them to become leader, and scans both stores for the payload; it then rebuilds the original holder the same way, waits, and scans again. It emits an entry_survival CA_EVENT carrying the reconstructed voter count, the acknowledgement outcome, the payload index, whether the payload remains on the holder after the rejoin, how many of the other voters hold it, the derived durable_on_majority with the copy count, and both terms.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; the committed configuration recorded in the node's own log is the basis on which a client acknowledgement is supposed to be durable.

comparisons.description: Three-voter case with the flag enabled: the reconstructed voter count is compared with the number of voters in the configuration entry persisted in the node's own log.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the reconstructed voter count matches the committed configuration entry.
Three-voter case with the flag enabled: an acknowledged commit is expected to be durable on a majority of the committed configuration rather than on a single copy.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the single running member of a three-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

before.description: Whether a reconstructed configuration smaller than the committed one changes which support counts. Seven in-process cases: the five previously exercised restart shapes (no-snapshot, snapshot-then-RemoveServer, and the within-flag case whose configuration entry stays above the replayed prefix) plus a new shape in which the snapshot records one voter because the second peer was demoted before it and the committed configuration afterwards has two voters because the peer was promoted again after it; that shape runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In the new shape, after the bounded leadership wait the other instance is stopped and one entry is committed with a 1000 ms Apply timeout, so the support the completed decision rested on is observable.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no membership change is issued after it.
In the new shape the committed configuration has two voters after the promotion while the node's own snapshot metadata still carries the demoted configuration with a single voter.

Every instance of the cluster is stopped before the restart in each case, so after the restart the other member is unavailable in the new shape as well and the surviving instance is the only member of the committed configuration that is running.
The bounded leadership window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms) and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, restarting more than one member, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.

parameters.cases: no_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_after_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_above_replayed_prefix flag-on, voter_promoted_after_snapshot flag-on/flag-off

experiments.revision_reason: Adds the three-voter lost_acknowledged_commit case with its flag-disabled control: demote both peers, snapshot the single-voter configuration, promote both peers again, restart the former leader, acknowledge one uniquely named commit on it, then bring the other two voters back and scan every store for that payload. Replaces the comparison set with this case's reconstruction and durability predicates.
